_readme: Every setting for the CYD ticker app. Edit, then reload it WITHOUT
Read through the shared appcfg.h loader. Any key may be left out -- the
firmware default applies. A value outside its allowed range is REJECTED and
named on the serial log, not silently clamped, so a typo tells you about
Logo size is NOT here, at either size: the firmware and tools/make-logos.py
have to agree on 24 and 128. Wi-Fi credentials are not here either, and
deliberately so -- this file is plain text on a filesystem anyone holding
the board can dump. See SECURITY.md.
_brightness: This board has an LDR, so brightness tracks the ROOM rather than the clock.
That deletes the C6's night.from/night.to pair outright -- and with it the
bug where night dimming only took effect if somebody pressed a button after
auto         follow the LDR. Set false to pin the backlight at 'max'.
min, max     the range the LDR maps between, 8-255. The floor is 8 rather
than 0 because 0 reads as a dead board.
closedScale  percent of the computed level to use while the market is shut,
10-100. A dark room and a closed market are different reasons
to dim, so they are different settings: the rows genuinely do
not change between the close and the next open, or at weekends.
_layout: list     six rows -- logo badge, symbol, sparkline, price, change
heatmap  3x4 grid of twelve tiles tinted by the size of the move
A STARTING POINT only. Changing layout on the device is stored in NVS,
which then wins over this key. The boot log says which is in effect.
DETAIL is not listed because it is not a layout you start in -- you get
there by tapping a stock, and leave by tapping LIST.
_timing: pageSeconds  how long each page of six rows stays up, 2-600.
cascadeMs    per-row stagger when a page flips, 0-400. Set 0 for an
instant flip; 22 reads as movement and costs nothing extra.
Note the page timer is FROZEN while a touch is held, so a tap can never
land on one symbol and resolve to the one that replaced it.
_sparkline: Yahoo's granularity for the intraday series, which is the same request the
price already comes from -- the series is free, but the PAYLOAD is not.
15m  ~26 points, much smaller, visibly coarser shape.
30m  ~13 points. For long watchlists on a tight heap.
Whatever this says, parse with a streaming filter over
indicators.quote[0].close and meta. Never hold the whole document.
_detail: The per-stock page, reached by tapping a row or a heatmap tile.
returnSeconds  auto-return to the list after this long, 0-3600. 0 never
returns. A panel parked on one stock shows you less than it
refreshOnOpen  jump the tapped symbol to the front of the fetch queue, so
a five-minute-old price refreshes while you are looking at
it. This is a priority in the existing queue, not an extra
request path, and it still obeys the rate floor.
_logos: rowBadges  draw the 24px logo beside each list row.
The badge is recognition, not identification -- the symbol text stays next
to it either way. A wordmark is an unreadable smudge at 24px, which is why
make-logos.py runs its percent-visible check at BOTH sizes and why a
missing small logo is a non-event rather than an error.
_refresh: Minutes between price refreshes. Stocks cost one HTTPS request EACH; coins
all travel in a single CoinGecko request and are nearly free.
The fetch loop runs on core 0 so it never stalls the UI -- but fetches stay
strictly SEQUENTIAL regardless, because each TLS session is ~40KB of a
520KB heap. Two cores do not buy you two sessions. The floor of roughly one
request per symbol per minute stands: Yahoo's 429 does not care how many
openMinutes    while the market is open, 1-240.
closedMinutes  while it is shut, 1-1440. Hourly is plenty.
coinMinutes    crypto, 1-240. Never closes, so this stays live overnight.
_timezone: POSIX TZ string, used for the clock AND for the market window below.
Default is US Eastern, which is where the listed exchanges are.
_market: Trading window as HH:MM, evaluated in the timezone above, Mon-Fri. It
drives both brightness.closedScale and the refresh interval. Change the
timezone and you must move these too -- that coupling is why they are
settings rather than a buried constant. An inverted window is rejected.
_symbols: Six rows show at once in list layout, twelve tiles in heatmap. 32 symbols
maximum, labels capped at 5 characters because that is the width of the
coins   CoinGecko ids (the id, not the ticker). Find one at
The logo fetcher looks coins up by LABEL, which has to be a real
ticker for a logo to be found.
